slides.0.title: Where the vineyards are: geography and terroir
slides.0.subtitle: Africa's northernmost country keeps its wine in the north
slides.1.title: All in the north
slides.1.highlights.0.title: The legal map
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The areas in the international register all lie in northern governorates such as Nabeul, Tunis, Bizerte and Béja. The dry south and the Sahara have no appellations
slides.1.highlights.1.title: The Cap Bon peninsula
slides.1.highlights.1.content: A peninsula reaching into the Mediterranean south-east of the capital, in Nabeul governorate. Kélibia is near its north-eastern tip and Sidi Salem near Grombalia at its base
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Inland
slides.1.highlights.2.content: West of the capital lies Tébourba on the lower Medjerda; further west, Thibar in Béja governorate is the region furthest from the sea
slides.1.content: Remember the directions: the Cap Bon peninsula, south of the capital, the northern valleys, and further west the inland hills.
slides.2.title: A Mediterranean climate
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The basic pattern
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Hot, dry summers and winter rain. Rainfall falls from north to south, and the vineyards sit in the wetter north
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The sea's influence
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Cap Bon is surrounded by sea on three sides, and sea breezes temper the summer heat. This is one reason the peninsula suits Muscat
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Thibar is different
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Secondary sources describe Thibar as more continental and shaped by altitude. Rainfall figures for each region are mostly unsourced, so this course does not ask you to learn them
slides.2.content: The sea and altitude are the two things northern Tunisia uses against the heat.
slides.3.title: Soils, and terroir in the law
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Common descriptions of the soils
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Kélibia is often described as siliceous sand, Sidi Salem as alluvium with gravel, and Coteaux d'Utique as limestone slopes. These come from secondary sources and are not tested
slides.3.highlights.1.title: How the law defines it
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Article 2 of Law 99-57 of 1999: an AOC draws its value from its geographical environment, made up of natural and human factors
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Natural factors include
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Soil, water, plant cover and climate. The human factors are local production methods, which must come from old, stable and well-known traditions
slides.3.content: Tunisian law spells out what terroir is made of, which is a good starting point before the regulations.
slides.4.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge check
In which governorate does the Kélibia area lie?
The international register gives a delimited area within Kélibia and Tazerka, in Nabeul governorate.
Which region lies in Béja governorate, furthest from the sea?
Muscat de Thibar is registered for Saint Joseph de Thibar, in Béja governorate.
Under Law 99-57, what do the natural factors of an AOC include?
B. The size of the winery
C. Soil, water, plant cover and climate
Article 2. The human factors are local production methods.
